correctness.rationale: Exact circular Dirichlet representation gives tagged Beta/Uniform splitting. Neighboring exponential two-sum joint tail is 2exp(-u)-exp(-2u); all nonneighbors are independent. Independent length-(log n)^2 blocks separated by one deleted index have vanishing double-exceedance probability and converge as rare marked blocks to the product-intensity Poisson process. The exponential total and partial sums transfer the law to circular positions and normalized Voronoi lengths. Chen–Stein and a Chebyshev sandwich prove the stated fixed-x O((1+loglog n)/log n) TV bound. The finite checker verifies independent identities but is not used as an asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The novel unit is the joint spatial/height/skew marked Poisson process and maximum-cell mark independence, not the classical unmarked Gumbel marginal. The full inspected modern primary texts concern largest empty regions or typical cells, and available older abstracts concern unmarked m-spacing counts. An older full-text access gap remains a material priority risk. An existing exact finite-size joint Voronoi cell-length vector law is a stronger precursor: in odd dimensions it reconstructs all gaps and hence implicitly covers every finite-n shape-mark distribution. It does not state or imply the present marked extreme Poisson process without new nontrivial asymptotic estimates; the one-dependent rare-event analysis and count approximation supply these. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: Maximal Voronoi-cell size controls worst-case allocation to one sampling site. The asymmetry of its two constituent gaps distinguishes an extreme cell caused by one long empty arc from one with balanced long arcs; this conditional geometric shape is not determined by the marginal Gumbel law or unmarked count approximations. A full marked Poisson law yields both spatial rare-cell diagnostics and the independent uniform shape of the worst cell; the fixed-threshold count rate aids calibration.
